evals.name: work-auto-selects-one-item-via-seam-claim
evals.expected_output: Reclaims stale leases at session start (idempotent), auto-selects exactly ONE item from the frontier (open, unblocked, unassigned) via the seam list-frontier, then acquires it through the seam claim verb (assignee + lease record, race-safe) before executing it. Autonomous execution defaults to orchestrator-dispatch — a scope-fenced implementation subagent in its own out-of-tree worktree, orchestrator never editing source. The seam claim is a non-optional prerequisite of dispatch: an external loop-prompt restating dispatch-in-a-worktree never substitutes for it, and dispatching before the claim is held is a defect. The claim identity is the authenticated session user, never the bot.
expectations: Runs an idempotent session-start reclaim (`work-item-tracker.sh reclaim`) before selecting — never releases a live lease
Selects exactly ONE item to work — never claims multiple at once
Selects from the frontier via `work-item-tracker.sh list-frontier` (open, `blocked_by_count == 0`, unassigned); `--autonomous` additionally excludes `needs-human`
Acquires via the seam `work-item-tracker.sh claim` (assignee + lease comment, same-identity aware) — NOT a `status:considering`/`status:claimed` label hold protocol
On a lost race (`claim` exit 7) advances to the next candidate rather than retrying the same item

Treats the seam claim (assignee + lease) as a non-optional prerequisite of dispatch — an external loop-prompt restating "dispatch in an out-of-tree worktree" does not substitute for it, and dispatching a subagent before the claim is held is a defect even when the loop-prompt never named the claim step

For autonomous execution, defaults to orchestrator-dispatch — dispatches a scope-fenced implementation subagent that edits in its own out-of-tree worktree (chaining to `/implementation:implement-dispatch` for mechanics, `/source-control:worktree` for the worktree), orchestrator never edits source; the interactive all-inline path is `/implementation:implement`
Whichever execution path runs, follows every step of the consuming project's development workflow first — no shortcuts, no skipped research

evals.name: work-excludes-and-cross-references-remapped-recurring-role
evals.prompt:
/work-items:work

The tracker binding maps recurring-maintenance to scheduled-upkeep. Both due maintenance and ordinary frontier items exist.
evals.expected_output: The work flow resolves recurring-maintenance to scheduled-upkeep before selection. It excludes scheduled-upkeep items from the non-recurring frontier tiers and uses scheduled-upkeep when listing open items for the recurring tiers. It never compares against or queries the default recurring literal.
expectations: Resolves the recurring-maintenance label before any tracker read
Excludes items carrying scheduled-upkeep from non-recurring frontier tiers
Uses --label scheduled-upkeep when cross-referencing recurring candidates
Does not fall back to the recurring literal after a valid remap

evals.name: work-dispatch-execution-pr-lifecycle-boundaries
evals.prompt:
/work-items:work

Run autonomously. The selected frontier item is a clean feature. After the worker's PR goes green, a reviewer leaves one VALID finding the team wants deferred rather than fixed in this branch.
evals.expected_output: The execute step runs orchestrator-dispatch: it spawns a scope-fenced implementation subagent in an out-of-tree worktree (chaining to /implementation:implement-dispatch and /source-control:worktree) and never edits source in the orchestrator. The dispatch brief carries the PR contract forward (referencing /source-control:pull-request, enumerating version bump + CHANGELOG + attribution trailer + Related + Closes #N). Concurrency and batch caps resolve from userConfig, not hardcoded literals, and a batch cap bounds a cycle, not the loop. Before opening the PR it does a full-diff read when the diff hits skill frontmatter/trigger keywords, cross-plugin contracts, or hooks. After CI green it runs one review pass; the deferred-but-valid finding is not resolved until a follow-up issue is filed via /work-items:track add and cited in the reply and Related. It then hands off to /source-control:babysit-prs and never merges.
expectations: Defaults to orchestrator-dispatch (scope-fenced subagent in an out-of-tree worktree, orchestrator never edits source), chaining to /implementation:implement-dispatch without re-describing its mechanics

The dispatch brief carries the PR contract by referencing /source-control:pull-request and enumerating version-bump / CHANGELOG / attribution-trailer / `## Related` / `Closes #N` — without a second PR-body definition
Concurrency and batch caps resolve from `${user_config.work_dispatch_concurrency_cap}` / `${user_config.work_cycle_batch_cap}` with no hardcoded literal; a batch cap bounds a cycle, not the loop
Does a full-diff read before opening a PR when the diff touches skill frontmatter descriptions/trigger keywords, cross-plugin contracts, or hooks
Does not resolve the VALID-but-deferred finding without a follow-up issue filed via /work-items:track add and cited in both the reply and `## Related`
Hands the PR off to /source-control:babysit-prs and never merges — work's lane ends at PR creation plus handoff
